text:
Massachusetts--Apparently only the Division of Fisheries and Game replied and had no objections to the statement.
<u>Mississippi</u>--Clearinghouse reports the proposed legislation to be consistent with present State goals and policies.
Missouri--Only the Water Resources Board had comments in response to the Clearinghouse. Their comment was that the statement was too general. An impact statement should be prepared for each species added to the list and the statement should include consideration of the effect of the Act as it relates to the human race.
Montana--Only the Department of Fish and Game responded to the State Clearinghouse request for comment on the EIS. Dissatisfaction with the EIS is due primarily to stronger Federal Authority for protection of endangered species. The Clearinghouse, otherwise, finds the statement adequate.
Minnesota--State review based only on comments received from the Department of Agriculture. The Department generally concurs with the statement but expresses reservations about attempting to alter the course of evolution.
Nebraska--The State Game and Parks Commission provided the only comment upon which State evaluation was based. The Commission neither endorses nor rejects the statement but proposes revision of the Bill to allow Federal assumption of protection only if the State does not first enact suitable legislation.
Nevada--Only comments forwarded were by the Department of Fish and Game which felt the States should have a stronger role than the proposed legislation provides.
North Carolina--Generally favorable although the State Board of Health has some apprehension that protection of endangered species may encourage some human vectors.
